newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-MAJOR PORTS REGISTER HIGHER H1 TURNOVER.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-MAJOR PORTS REGISTER HIGHER H1 TURNOVER.

text.p: Latvia's three major ports, Ventspils, Riga and Liepaja, saw a rise in their half-year turnover, reaching 25.2 million tonnes in total, the transport ministry said on Monday.

"We will try to maintain the current levels despite competition and the total turnover so far this year is in line with the planned 50 million tonnes for the whole of 1997," Transport Minister Vilis Kristopans told a news conference.
Ventpils, by far the busiest port in the region, registered 19.32 million tonnes of cargo, up by 1.15 million compared to the first six months of 1996.
Ventspils has earlier said it plans a 1997 throughput of 38 million tonnes or a rise by 2.3 million tonnes from 1996.
Riga port has shown the biggest owerall cargo increase to 4.8 million tonnes from 3.1 million.
Meanwhile, container volumes fell, due to increased competition from Lithuania's Klaipeda and Liepaja.
The fact that Riga lags behind neighbouring Tallinn and Klaipeda was also explained by a lack of port management.
"There still is a vacuum of power in the Riga harbour," Kristopans said.
Liepaja, succesfully recovering from being a closed Soviet navy base, reloaded 1.09 million tonnes of cargo during the first half-year against 808,000 tonnes in the correponding period of 1996.
